_comment: SITE COMMISSIONING TEMPLATE -- Automatrix PV-DG Controller.
Deliberately NOT ready to apply. Every value written as null must be measured
or supplied at the plant; the firmware will reject an incomplete configuration
rather than run on a plausible-looking guess, and that is the intended
Work through docs/SITE_COMMISSIONING_RUNBOOK.md while filling this in. Nothing
here should be copied from config-samples/lab-simulator.json: those are values
for a simulated plant and several of them would be actively wrong on real
The controller reports commissioning_scope = production only when every
commanded inverter has passed physical readback qualification. On this commit
no profile has, so a correctly filled template still yields a monitoring and
protection installation until qualification is done on site.

_notes: One meter per source. A grid meter is mandatory; a generator meter is needed
for generator-mode control. Confirm every address READ-ONLY with mbpoll
before writing anything (runbook section 2).
data_type: 0 uint16, 1 int16, 2 uint32, 3 int32, 4 float32.
Grid active power MUST be signed -- it goes negative when exporting, and an
unsigned type decodes export as a large import, which is the wrong sign at
the exact moment the controller must reduce PV.
word_order: 0 ABCD (high word first), 1 CDAB, 2 BADC, 3 DCBA. Prove it with
a known non-zero power rather than assuming; a wrong order can read plausibly
at some values and absurdly at others.
poll_ms: 0 means poll again as soon as the previous transaction completes.
Measure the gateway first (runbook) -- one site gateway sustained only about
11 requests per second with a ~300 ms stall on a quarter of transactions.
timeout_ms: must clear the MEASURED worst-case response, not the typical one.
A timeout inside the tail records healthy responses as failures, which feeds
the quality window that blocks control input.

meters._comment: Delete this entry if the site has no separate generator meter.
meters.name: Generator Meter

_notes: rated_kw is the nameplate rating and sets the fleet capacity the ramp rates
are a percentage of. Getting it wrong scales every ramp.
If a SmartLogger or any other gateway is in the Modbus path, unit_id is the
LOGGER's id for that inverter and need not match anything printed on the
machine. Confirm it by reading the model string back.
Choose the profile matching the ACTUAL manufacturer and model. Check
GET /api/inverter-profiles first: several profiles are refused by design and
the response states each one's write permission and why.
lab_target MUST be false for real equipment. Setting it true against a real
inverter is a false statement about physical reality, and it is the one thing
the design cannot defend against.
Known refusals at the time of writing -- read the live API rather than trusting
this list: GoodWe (command register is flash-backed with no documented write
rate, so commanding it would destroy the inverter's memory), Growatt (power-on
write lock, password redacted in the manual, re-arms after five minutes),
Chint/CPS and Knox/AISWEI (prerequisite enable register whose readability is
not established by any citation).
These are the generator-protection numbers and they cannot be guessed. Take
them from the genset nameplate and its controller settings, and record who
supplied them.
minimum_loading_percent protects the engine from wet stacking; reserve_kw and
reverse_power_margin_kw keep PV below the point where the genset sees reverse
power. The genset's OWN reverse-power trip setting and delay must be read and
recorded too -- the controller must act before that trip, not after it.
PARALLEL ENGINES. A site may run up to three gensets in parallel, and the
controller now holds a separate rating and minimum-loading figure for each.
The four generator_* fields below are engine 0. The 'generators' array below
them is engines 1 and 2 -- fill in one object per engine the site can
actually run, and leave an engine out of service if it cannot.
This matters arithmetically, not just for record keeping. The minimum-loading
floor is computed against the AGGREGATE rating of the engines measured online.
Commissioning one rating for a plant that can run two engines in parallel
makes that denominator wrong in the permissive direction: the controller would
allow far more PV than the plant can carry, which is the reverse-power
condition this product exists to prevent. Every engine the site can run needs
a rating and a minimum-loading figure, or the commissioning gate stays closed.
Give each engine its own generator-role meter and set that meter's
generator_index to the engine's slot number. Which engines are running is a
runtime fact and is read from those meters; it is not configuration. Without
per-engine meters a multi-engine plant cannot establish its running set and
the controller holds PV at zero.
REMAINING GAP: POST /api/solar-grid/config currently accepts engine 0 only.
Engines 1 and 2, load_sharing_mode and the per-engine roles and base-load
setpoints are persisted and enforced by the firmware but are not yet writable
over the HTTP API, so a multi-engine plant cannot be commissioned from the web
interface yet. Raise it with the product owner.
load_sharing_mode: HOW THE ENGINES DIVIDE THE LOAD. This is no longer assumed.
It decides WHICH engine sets the minimum-loading floor, so the floor is not
computable without it, and a plant that can run two or more engines keeps the
commissioning gate closed until this is set. Read it off the genset master
controller and record who confirmed it. One of:
"isochronous" -- proportional kW sharing. Every engine sits at the same
percentage of its own rating. The engine with the HIGHEST minimum-loading
percentage binds, and the floor is sum(rating) x that percentage.
"base_load" -- one or more engines held at a fixed kW setpoint by their own
governors, the rest absorbing the swing. Every in-service engine then needs a
role in the 'generators' array below, engine 0's role and setpoint go in
engine_0_role and engine_0_base_load_kw, every base-loaded engine needs its
setpoint, and at least one engine must be a swing engine. A base-loaded
engine whose setpoint is BELOW its own minimum loading is a commissioning
fault the controller reports rather than computes around: its load does not
follow the plant total, so no PV curtailment ever brings it up.
"droop" -- REFUSED. The firmware stores it and then keeps the gate closed.
A droop floor needs each governor's no-load speed trim and the running bus
frequency; the speed trim is not a number that can be read reliably off a
commissioned plant, and a load-sharing line or master controller usually
overrides the droop characteristic anyway. The honest conservative bound for
an unknown sharing law is that any engine may take an arbitrarily small
share, which permits no PV at all -- identical to refusing. If the site is
droop-shared, that is a plant question for the product owner, not a number
to enter here.
There is deliberately NO default. Base-load sharing can put the floor either
above or below the isochronous floor depending on the setpoints, so no mode is
conservative for every plant and none may be assumed. Unset means no PV.
base_load_tolerance_kw / base_load_tolerance_percent_of_rating: HOW FAR A
BASE-LOADED ENGINE MAY SIT FROM ITS SETPOINT BEFORE THE CONTROLLER STOPS
BELIEVING IT. Required only if at least one engine is base_load. Fill in either
one, or both.
Why it is required rather than optional. The minimum-loading floor for a
base-load plant is sum(setpoints) + sum(swing ratings) x worst swing minimum
loading percent. Its first term credits the base-loaded engines with the load
their setpoints promise. If a governor leaves kW control -- its load-sharing
line is lost, it is switched to droop, it reverts to isochronous, someone puts
it in manual -- the engine quietly becomes a swing engine and that term is
wrong in the PERMISSIVE direction: the controller believes load is being
absorbed that is not, and allows more PV than the plant can carry. That is the
reverse-power condition. The controller already measures each engine's power, so
it can see this happen; what it cannot do is decide by itself how much
disagreement is normal for your governors.
There is deliberately NO default, and the firmware does not invent one. No
manual or nameplate in this product states a figure, so it must come from the
plant: read the genset master controller's own kW load-sharing accuracy or
band, or observe the steady-state spread of measured power around the setpoint
on a commissioned engine, and record who supplied the number and how. Until it
is set, a plant with a base-loaded engine cannot be commissioned -- the gate
reports generator_base_load_tolerance_unset. A closed gate is recoverable in an
afternoon; over-generating into an under-loaded genset is not.
If BOTH are given the controller uses the NARROWER band. It is the only
conservative reading: this band sits on one side of one comparison, so widening
it can only make real drift harder to see.
Once it is set, disagreement beyond the band holds PV at zero and reports
base_load_setpoint_drift. The controller does NOT quietly re-treat that engine
as a swing engine and carry on: it knows the governor is not doing what it was
commissioned to do and knows nothing about what it is doing instead. A stale or
missing measurement on a base-loaded engine likewise holds PV at zero rather
than reading as agreement -- unknown is not confirmation.
Leave enabled false until the commissioning gate reports satisfied AND you
have read its scope. A satisfied gate with scope lab_simulator_only is not a
production release.
interval_ms: 10..10000. Fixed, not poll-on-completion -- a jittering period
gives a jittering integral term. 20 ms suits a link answering in tens of
milliseconds; slow it if the measured gateway cannot keep up.
meter_stale_timeout_ms must be >= interval_ms and should exceed the measured
worst-case acquisition latency, or fresh data will intermittently be judged
stale and control will be inhibited for no real reason.
grid_ramp disabled = step straight to the allowed target after
synchronisation, which is the grid-mode requirement. generator_ramp enabled
with down_pct_s GREATER than up_pct_s: give power away slowly, take it back
quickly.
kp/ki are plant-specific. Start conservative and observe for oscillation;
passing the gate's tuning check only proves the values are in range, not that
the loop is stable.
